text:
sam_sales: Quick question — running a presales POC with a fintech customer. They want streaming SSE + function/tool-calling with structured JSON events. Handshake intermittently fails on token refresh, client sees 403 mid-stream. Anyone seen this?

ira_engineer: Hey Sam — couple checks: 1) are they using ephemeral creds or a long-lived API key? 2) which SDK (js/go/python) and transport (native websocket vs SSE)?

sam_sales: JS SDK (browser embed for demo) + SSE fallback. Using short-lived credentials via our demo token rotation flow.

devon_se: Browser+SSE+ephemeral is tricky. If the stream outlives token TTL and client tries to refresh mid-stream, server rejects. For a demo we recommend either: 1) proxy that mints ephemeral tokens and reconnects, or 2) use websocket SDK which supports in-band reconnects gracefully.

jen_ops: Also verify CORS and preflight. SSE requires proper Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Allow-Credentials if cookies are used.

sam_sales: Customer also wants tool-calls emitted as distinct structured events so downstream systems can react. Is that supported in streaming mode?

ira_engineer: Yes. We emit discrete events for tool lifecycle. Example SSE payloads: 

```
event: token
data: {"type":"tool_call_start","tool":"account_lookup","call_id":"abc123"}

event: message
data: {"type":"assistant_fragment","role":"assistant","content":"..."}

event: tool
data: {"type":"tool_call_result","call_id":"abc123","payload":{"status":"ok","account_id":42}}
```

ira_engineer: Client should parse per-event JSON lines. Our JS SDK provides an onTool callback that normalizes across SSE/ws transports.

devon_se: If they want a single final JSON array, we can emit a `final` event with assembled structure, but per-event consumption is simpler and lower latency.

sam_sales: Pricing concerns — does streaming increase cost and do tool calls count as tokens?

jen_ops: Billing is per-token identical for streamed and non-streamed responses. Tool calls: tokens consumed by the model are billed. Outbound external API calls are not billed by Redwood. If they use our managed embeddings/search, those calls are billed under embeddings.

sam_sales: Security asks: SOC2, BYOK/KMS, IP allowlist, SAML SSO for console.

devon_se: SOC2 docs are available in our compliance pack. BYOK/KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted can integrate with customer-managed keys in supported regions but requires support request. IP allowlist and SAML SSO are enterprise features; needs SAML metadata and admin list.

sam_sales: Any blockers we should flag for the PoC?

ira_engineer: Potential blockers:
- Browser SSE with ephemeral tokens (no reconnect flow)
- CORS misconfig on demo origin
- BYOK before demo requires org-level infra/legal work (slow)
- On-prem routing needs Private deployment (long lead)

jen_ops: Ops: if they plan for high QPS enable burst override on the trial Dedicated pool, otherwise throttling/429s expected.

sam_sales: Short-term plan to unblock demo this week?

devon_se: 1) Switch demo to websocket SDK for stable reconnection. 2) Proxy token refresh through a tiny lambda returning fresh ephemeral tokens and force reconnect when TTL < 30s. 3) Use onTool callback to parse tool events. 4) Escalate BYOK if customer insists, but not required for demo.

ira_engineer: Snippet for reconnect logic:

```js
// pseudo: reconnect when token nearly expired
async function startStream(){
  let token = await fetch('/mint-token').then(r=>r.text());
  const ws = new WebSocket(`wss://api.redwood.ai/stream?token=${token}`);
  ws.onmessage = e => handleEvent(JSON.parse(e.data));
  ws.onclose = async ()=> setTimeout(startStream, 500);
}
startStream();
```

sam_sales: Can someone own the demo checklist and join customer call Thursday 10am PST?

devon_se: I can join and own SDK bits.

jen_ops: I'll cover ops/pricing and request burst quota for the trial.

ira_engineer: I'll build the token proxy sample.

sam_sales: Great — pre-demo run Wednesday 2pm PT. I'll send invites and the POC checklist.
